learning_outcomes.text: Understand problems and technical solutions to operate a communication system.
Understand the impact of the environment and the service type on the preferable solution.
Describe the main commercial systems with reference to the studied techniques.
Know the physical principles that affect a transmission system.
Know the transmission techniques and their effectiveness in the presence of physical phenomena.
Understand the effects of the interaction between different users and services.
Understand the reasons behind the choices of different techniques in different systems.
Know the performance that can be achieved and the factors influencing them.
Analyze requirements and consequently adopt a conscious choice based on the requested service.

syllabus_topics: Propagation phenomena and how to design efficient transmission techniques to counteract transmission impairments
Review of transmission techniques (analog and digital)
Transmission of baseband digital data: robustness to noise and bandwidth efficiency
Introduction to traffic theory for performance characterization and system planning
Transition matrix and state probabilities for Markov systems
Circuit switched networks: space, time and hybrid circuit switched nodes
Signaling, in-band, out-of band, common channel
Multiplexing in circuit switched networks frequency (FDM)
The data Link Layer: line management, link configuration, packet extraction, error control (FEC and ARQ)
Distributed multiplexing in packet networks: Aloha, Slotted-Aloha, CSMA/*, Token passing
Wired and Wireless Local Area Networks (LAN) in the IEEE 802 set of standards
Historical perspective, Frame relay and ATM networks
Evolution and convergence to IP based networks
Coding and transmission of digital video
Network architectures for video distribution (DVB, CDN)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral part. The written part comprises 4 questions to be answered in 1 hour. Admission to the oral exam requires a grade of at least 8 in the written test. The oral exam must also achieve a grade of at least 8 to pass. The final grade is the sum of grades from the oral and written parts (max grade written 17, max grade oral 17).
bibliography: J. Kurose, K. Ross, "Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach." Pearson
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Informatica (Electronic And Computer Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
